title: Adaptive Honest Interval Length for ATE under a Cross-Stratum Confounding Budget
banked_reason: D0.5 math PASS, but kernel_substituted@oeq:uniform-frontier: universal deterministic allocation-adaptive frontier remains open; cold tier incremental, field floor unmet, score ceiling 5.9 below 7.4.
gap_reasons: The proposed universal, allocation-adaptive frontier with an attaining interval is still open; the delivered fixed-positive-design bracket is a strictly weaker kernel and cannot serve as that headline deliverable.

I_band is only conditionally reduced to an LP at fixed (nu,e); without a finite end-to-end endpoint optimization or evaluable algorithm, the claimed observable interval does not yet clear the universal usability gate.

Position the fixed-design bracket theorem itself against the closest adaptive-interval and finite-sample Gaussian-ATE results (including the listed Luo--Gao, Cho--Luo--Gao, and Armstrong--Kolesar comparators), stating precisely what their results do not supply and what this bracket newly supplies.
proof_attempt_summary: The D-stage established mathematically sound normalized density-band results, an honest observable CDF interval, fixed-positive-design confidence-length bounds, and selected occupancy obstructions. The decision review found that these do not prove the promised universal deterministic, allocation-adaptive frontier; its exact multicell occupancy transition and finite end-to-end interval optimization remain open. The independent novelty review estimated incremental tier, below the field floor.
tldr: A single population bound on uncontrolled selection couples maternal-covariate strata in a copula-robust Gaussian-marginal causal model. The note proves exact normalized-band realization, a legal joint two-point lower modulus, a finite-sample honest CDF interval with an explicit Kolmogorov allocation length bound, and, for every fixed positive-cell design with \(B>0\), the confidence-length bracket \(G(\eta,B)\leq\liminf_n\sqrt{2\log n}\,L_{n,\alpha}(\eta;B)\leq\limsup_n\sqrt{2\log n}\,L_{n,\alpha}(\eta;B)\leq2\sqrt{2}\,G(\eta,B)\). The design-uniform triangular-array frontier and exact deterministic multicell occupancy boundary remain unresolved.
gap: Scalar same-law adaptive intervals do not allocate one sensitivity budget across strata, while fixed-fraction covariate bounds optimize a different bounded-outcome identification problem. The missing result is a sharp inference frontier for a point-identified Gaussian ATE when both confounding placement and sampling information are jointly allocated.
fill: The project derives an evaluable joint allocation object, certifies finite-sample honesty, constructs legal lower pairs, characterizes pooling strictness, and asks for a shared-multiplier test inversion that attains the same frontier uniformly.
